title: HOI4 Live Tools campaign plan
description: plan.json for the standing-plan executor (native/src/plan_run.rs) and the player. Every top-level key carries x-owner: executor (the executor reads it today) or player (the player acts on it from the brief). Inside an executor-owned key every key has one reader too: executor (inherited when unmarked), lint (only the planning tools read it: it shapes estimates, the executor does not act on it), text (for people; why and note are text unmarked) or, with x-executor-planned, a key whose executor step is still to come. scripts/hoi4facts/plan_keys.py check fails when a key has no reader. x-executor-planned names the build item (coverage audit section 6, W1-n / W2-n) whose executor step takes a player key over; the owner flips to executor when that step lands (x-planned-owner is the older marker). Unknown top-level keys are errors except _-prefixed ones. tests/test_plan_schema.py keeps this file in step with plan_run.rs.

multiplayer.description: the multiplayer game's rules: switch -> allowed; wins over roleplay and the FAIR defaults in the lint, the guard and the run result

roleplay.description: a roleplay instruction's switches: switch -> allowed; wins over the FAIR defaults, loses to multiplayer, in the lint, the guard and the run result

_rules.description: rule-set switches, read by the FAIR plan lint, by the server's FAIR guard on every action (native/src/fair_guard.rs) and reported in the run result (`rules`), layered: a multiplayer game's rules win over a roleplay instruction, which wins over the FAIR defaults (native/src/fair_guard.rs FAIR_DEFAULTS). Guarded rules (naval_mines, access, factions, timing, space_marines, paratroopers, submarines) are off by default: true lifts the guard. Allowances: collaboration, volunteers, air_volunteers, lend_lease, attaches, eben_emael_raid, propaganda, strategic_bombing_war_support on by default; paradrops and refinery_bombing off by default (a roleplay goal or META turns them on)

campaign.description: campaign identity; plan_state.json is ignored for another campaign

edits.description: Logged key edits made to a strategist plan after it was made (a live engineer's fix between runs or at a segment boundary): each names the keys, the date, who and why, so the strategist can take the finding into the next plan.

decision_departures.description: The restore-or-justify record against the run's sourced decision table (RUN/decisions.md): each table row the plan does not follow, with the game fact or arithmetic that forbids it and what the plan does instead (lint decisions.coverage; a lint is never the reason).

execution_rule.description: the numbers of execution auto (every key optional)

supply_floor.description: share of a division's supply need a stretch's carry feeds it at; default 0.5

hold_ratio.description: divisions a stretch keeps against each hostile division seen facing it; default 1.0

slack.description: divisions a front may stand over its room (with another as far under) before the prepare spreads again; default a fifth of the divisions on the fronts, at least 3

over_cap.description: at war, from the third day of the war on, a front standing over its room by the slack sends its surplus sideways to the army's front with most room (one move per refinement cool-down, the largest first); default true

capacity.description: fronts by attack capacity (by command, a unit with two or more fronts): each front's weight in the spread is what its stretch can fight with and feed (the width its battles take from the directions we border them, the supply reaching it, the hostile divisions seen facing it), not its length; in the prepare a spread far from that is spread again; at war the reserve of a battle beyond its engaged divisions moves sideways to the front with most room (within refine_days). false switches it off

min_hours.description: hours a battle stands not won before its unused sides attack it; default 72

days.description: days before the same battle is pushed again; default 5

divisions.description: the most divisions one push sends; default 6

shed.description: with no stuck battle to push, the divisions waiting where they cannot fight (the reserve of a full or over-reserved battle, the fit idle ones on the line) attack the unattacked enemy province beside them, within the army's refinement cool-down, after the opening's own orders (every attacker executing, its mode read); default false (off until a leg proves it raises the engaged share)

push.description: THE STUCK POINT (default on): once a game day at war, a battle of ours that has stood min_hours, is not being won and has width to spare, bordered by own provinces whose fit divisions stand idle, is attacked from those sides by a direct order (hoi4_army_move with the divisions); one battle in days; false switches it off

armour_ground.description: default true: at war a spearhead formation whose divisions wait in the reserves of rough-ground battles (terrain or river penalty, forts) leaves the state the operation gave it to the infantry (the plan's own thrust is kept), and its next objective is the state of the line or the enemy's contact its armour reaches cheapest by the ground model, not the nearest

stall_days.description: game days without a province gained on the current line before the next line is drawn (default 7)

stacking.description: default on; false (or {enabled: false}) turns it off. Once the attack executes, no province holds more of the operation's line, wing and group divisions than its supply feeds and a battle's width takes (max_per_province, default 11); a starving province (supply below 35%) seen in two supply reads is thinned to what feeds its divisions at 50% supply (at most half of them), most worn infantry first and at most a third of an army at once, into one second echelon army per line army with an area defence of its station (an empty state of the enemy border, else the nearest state behind the line; station overrides); it is fed forward when the line has room or its army is worn, and rejoins its army when the operation ends

by_width.description: true: each own front province holds no more of the line's divisions than the battles it faces take with profit (terrain width plus support width per extra direction, the divisions' template width, the over-width and stacking penalties of the defines), and the divisions a battle read shows waiting beyond the width are surplus too (attacking or not); the surplus forms the second echelon, fed forward only into room the battles have or to relieve a worn army. Before the war the line's capacity is noted once a game day (no order)

keep.description: with by_width: divisions each front province keeps over its battles' fit (default 0)

battle_reserve.description: with by_width: divisions a battle's reserve keeps, the freshest (default 0: a reserve joins only by over-filling the width)

thin_at_war.description: true: at war the surplus is taken out into a second echelon as above. Default false: at war no division is taken off its order (each one moved arrives with planning 0); the stack is noted and the deep line keeps the front spread. An echelon that exists is still fed forward

orders_by.description: command: the operation's orders carry exact provinces for the in-process army commands (a front with against + own_states, one order per stretch; a spearhead with target_provinces under its front's id; an arrow that misses its line gets a new path on the same order with replace_order, keeping the order and its planning bonus, never a delete or a clear). Default: command when the run posts both in-process battle-plan families (orders and orders2), else mouse. mouse keeps the mouse path on such a run

axis_by.description: terrain: every mobile formation with its own front takes its path by the ground model (see formations[].offensive.axis_by)

planning_gate.description: the operation reads as ready (its declaration goes out) only once the attacking armies' planning bonus, weighted by divisions, reaches share (0.9) of cap (0.3, PLANNING_MAX) or has stopped growing for two game days; a dated declaration waits for it at most max_wait_days (7) past its date

spear_pockets.description: true: the pocket order for spearheads: the two spearheads nearest a one-neck pocket (hoi4_encirclement_candidates) are painted to its neck state, the arms of a closed ring keep their orders while the group reduces it, a neck not closed in 6 days is given up. Not with strike formations in the operation. pockets false switches it off

flank_guard.description: true: a second echelon's station is the deepest state of a spearhead's axis we hold (the corridor behind the armour)

deadline_days.description: {TAG: days}: each small enemy's deadline from the day its war began

ratio.description: the divisions the armies facing an enemy should have per hostile division seen in its border states (default 2)

opening.description: several small enemies in one window: while the armies facing one are under ratio:1 against the hostile divisions seen in its border states, or its deadline has passed with it still in the war, the operation's largest second echelon goes to the army facing it with the most room (merged, else the part that fits); at most two sends per enemy, one a game day

assault_guard.description: default true. A wing (an army attacking on its own, not armour) never starts its attack alone: it executes once an attack of the same war executes (or an army of the operation attacks into the same states), and an executing order is never stopped by the guard. "odds": it also waits for twice the enemy divisions seen in the target's border states (or a second direction, or 21 days of the joint attack). false: no guard

refine_days.description: game days an army rests from the operation's refinements at war once one acted on it (default 5): a width thinning out of it, an echelon fed into it, an opening send into it, a supply stop of it. Each takes divisions off their orders or stops the plan, so it acts at most once in this many days per army

deep_line.description: default true when orders go by command: a plain offensive's target line is the far edge of its line's states seen from our border (the coast, the far border, the back of the last state; every line state keeps a province, none on our border), sent as exact provinces, so the whole front advances through the country instead of converging on the few provinces a stroke between two state centres reads back. A target the module or the game does not take is drawn by the stroke in the same call. false: the stroke

pockets.description: default true. The pocket order: from the encirclement read the best pocket two strike formations can cut off is chosen, both march at its neck, the ring is held while the group reduces it, then the armour returns to its objectives (counted in op:pockets_closed). false: the strike formations never leave their objectives for a pocket

wing_stall.description: default false. true: a wing that stood WING_STALL_DAYS at war with no state of its line taken gives the line's first state up (to the group or a pocket) and attacks the next one: its orders are cleared once (every division's planning goes with them), the front is clicked at the new line and the offensive drawn again. Default: a stalled wing keeps its line and its planning

regroup_at_war.description: true: the group is formed again with the line armies outside it (and reserves released to the operation) while the country is at war with someone else, as long as the operation's own enemies are not at war with us; an army in another group joins too; never an army another running operation owns or one standing in contact with an enemy. Default false: the regroup runs only while the country is at war with nobody

reserve_orders.description: true: the operation owns its `reserve` armies and gives each a standing order: a whole-army march to its station, then a fallback line through the row's `fallback` states, else an area defence of the station; on `release_when` a row `to: "operation"` is cleared and joins the group at its next regroup, a row to a hold keeps its standing order. Default false: reserve rows are text

marshals.description: generals for the operation's army groups: a group without a field marshal (a regroup or the second group of a split forms a new game group, which has none) gets the first of them who leads no other group (hoi4_army_commander; a general is promoted for command power). Absent: the operation gives no group a marshal

group_cap.description: the line armies one army group takes (the game's field marshal cap is 5). With more line armies than this the operation fights in TWO groups split by geography: the front's own states are halved along the line between the two farthest apart, each half of the line armies (by where they stand) is formed into its own group, and each group draws one front on its own piece of the border (hoi4_army_front from_states) and carries one offensive through its side of the line (and of the far line and every later line). Absent: one group whatever the number

replace_arrows.description: true: an arrow that misses its unit's line is deleted alone (hoi4_army_plan delete_order: the front and its planning bonus stay) before the new one is drawn; at war an arrow that will not delete alone clears the unit's orders once and front and arrow are drawn again. x-grammar: string     := comparison | flag | date | ""       ("" holds always)
comparison := name[:arg] op value   (spaces around op optional; op is < <= > >= == !=)
flag       := name[:arg]            (a yes/no atom: x-atoms kind bool; negate with {"not": ...})
date       := YYYY.MM.DD | date:YYYY.MM.DD   (reached; same as date >= YYYY.MM.DD)
value      := number -?D[.D][%] for kind number; a date for kind date; a TAG for kind tag
kind tag   := owner|controller|state_controller:<state>, province_controller:<province> with == or != TAG
(a single = is ==: the older owner:<state>=<TAG> form)
ratio      := atoms with ratio: true are fractions 0..1; a value above 1, or written with %, is a percent
arg        := province|state: digits; tag: [A-Z][A-Z0-9]{2}; key: [A-Za-z0-9_.-]+; id: [A-Za-z0-9_]+;
branch: army|air|navy (land, naval accepted); army: an army or army_layout name_hint (no < > = !
and no edge spaces); equipment: [A-Za-z0-9_]+; name: [A-Za-z0-9_.@^:]+ (script variable)
evaluation := three-valued: an atom that cannot be read now is unknown, never true, and whatever waits on
it waits; all is false when one part is false, else unknown when one is unknown; any is the
x-atoms    := every atom: kind, arg, min/max, ratio, unit, the read that answers it; readable: false marks
the atoms that are always unknown today (lint predicates.unreadable); legacy_of names the
current atom an older spelling stands for
predicate.description: A check on the game state, as native/src/plan_predicate.rs parses it: a string `atom op value` (ops < <= > >= == !=) or a bare yes/no atom, combined as {"all":[...]}, {"any":[...]}, {"not": p} (a plain list is all). x-grammar is the grammar, x-atoms the atom table; hoi4facts/validate.py parse_predicate implements both.

call.description: The exact tool call a player-owned item stands for (lint: player items list a tool call).

enabled.description: false switches the war executive off (default on when war is an object)

land_orders.description: false: the executor gives no land orders (no war step, no layout marches, no hold posts); the armies' own battle plans as drawn carry the land war, while declarations, air, supply and the economy still run

first.description: false runs the war step after the economy steps (default: war first)

enemies.description: count only while at war with them (hoi4_wars validated)

min_army.description: divisions an army needs to be driven (default 6)

cooldown_hours.description: game hours between orders to one army (default 12)

reserve.description: army names the executor never drives into an attack or a move: a reserve still holds the state it stands in with a front on the enemy-held land beside it (a guard of that state), so a second front is never left empty

player_claim_seconds.description: an army the player ordered within this many seconds is left alone (default 300)

axes.description: ordered target state lists; an army follows the axis whose next enemy-held state is nearest (an army_layout role with an axis follows its own axis first); an explicit empty list is a hold phase: no attack on enemy land, own states are still retaken

theatre.description: own states an army must stand in to be driven

guard_states.description: the first army standing in such a state guards it

guards.description: army name -> own state it holds (never attacks)

motorization.description: supply trucks level set once on every driven army

execution.description: how the driven armies' battle plans are carried out (hoi4_army_plan mode), set once per army when it has its lines and before its first execute order: careful (no attack on heavily fortified provinces, none that lengthens the front), balanced (the game's default), rush (every province of the plan is attacked: it suits a weak or broken enemy line, lengthens the front and can gather an army in one province without supply). Absent: the game's default stands and nothing is sent

strike.description: Objective strikes: true or an object switches the war step from battle plans to one march order of a whole army on one province at a time, once the opening plans have done their work. Per army the objective is its first vp_targets row not yet held (the first province of the row's path that is not held) when the army stands beside it or on the path; else an enemy victory point with `beside` fresh divisions next to it; else a march to the first province of the row's path (the assembly point); else the nearest enemy victory point no other army strikes. The order is sent once; the next objective is ordered the tick the last one falls. A strike whose divisions beside the objective fall under `rest` of their best organisation, or that lasts `max_days`, ends: the objective is closed for the army (`rest_days` after a worn strike, `close_days` after one that stood or a second worn one) and its next march order replaces the attack; with `halt` true it is halted instead and the army strikes again at `resume` or after `rest_days`. While on, battle plans, pocket fall-back, rests, stall answers, the overdrawn rule and command merges do not act on the driven armies; guard armies keep their fronts unless `guards` is true; `reserve` armies and armies the player ordered lately are left alone.

after_vp.description: victory points of the enemies the player must hold before the step takes the armies over; until then the battle plans run

reopen.description: an army with every objective in reach closed reopens the one it would choose without the closures instead of standing idle (the worn gate still holds back a worn army)

halt.description: true: a strike that ends is halted and the army rests where it stands. Default: no halt order; the objective is closed for the army (rest_days after a worn strike, close_days after one that stood) and its next march order replaces the attack. A halted division walks back to the front line its army still holds

feed.description: outside a strike, a stack its province cannot feed (floor of the divisions' need) sends its most worn divisions to held land near it with room for them

garrison.description: a taken victory point at the front keeps the most worn division of the army standing in it

stack.description: at most this many divisions strike or assemble from one province (0: no limit)

widen.description: divisions a strike left over take the enemy provinces beside the army, two at a time; land that fed fewer than two divisions when own divisions last stood in it is not taken this way

cover.description: divisions a formation keeps on each own state it covers (army_layout covers and guard_states_in_order, and the states of its tasks, sized by the task's count) while that state touches land the enemy holds; the rest strike. A guard formation holds its covered states with every division, spread over the exposed ones, and stands still where nothing faces it. 0: no posts

stall_rush.description: true: the first answer to an executing plan that took no ground for stall_days is the rush execution mode (once per army; the plan keeps executing and keeps its planning bonus, the stall clock starts again), and only the next stall goes on to replans, the second direction and the direct move. Not when execution is rush already. Default false: a stall goes straight to them. Rush suits a weak or broken enemy line; it attacks every province of the plan, lengthens the front and can gather an army in one unsupplied province, so it costs a stall period only where the plan asks for it

stall_days.description: game days without progress on a target (no new main state and no province taken in the target or the state the army stands in) before the stall response: the executing plan is stopped and planned again (replans), then a second direction, then a direct move with a back-off (default 8); with stall_rush true the rush execution mode comes first

replans.description: times a stalled executing offensive is stopped and planned again on one target (the army regains organisation and planning bonus on its line and executes through the planning wait) before the second direction and the direct move (default 2; 0 goes straight to them)

rest_below.description: absolute organisation below which an army rests; replaces rest_below_pct when set (no default: the share rule applies)

resume_above.description: absolute organisation at which a rested army resumes; replaces resume_above_pct when set (no default: the share rule applies)

fill_floor.description: mean equipment fill (0.9 or 90) of an army's divisions (hoi4_supply equipment_fill_min) below which it gets no new attack order and does not resume after a rest; 0 turns the gate off (default 0.9: every missing 1% of equipment costs about 1% attack)

supply_floor.description: supply percent (50 or 0.5) below which an executing army rests and no army gets a new attack order, except a move to retake an own state (default 50)

rest_max_days.description: a rested army resumes anyway after this many game days when its supply is above supply_hold (default 20)

direct_moves.description: true: direct hoi4_army_move orders instead of battle plans (a victory-point target is then a province move); false: a victory-point target names the state of the battle plan's offensive

supply_first.description: false: do not raise supply lines in the construction queue

avoid_pockets.description: false: do not pull encircled armies back

posture.description: defend: a defender until its counter-attack phase. In a hold phase (axes: []) no army draws a line on enemy land and none retakes a lost own state (a retake is an attack); the armies stand where the layout, the guards and the defence lines put them and entrench; every other theatre army keeps one front on the contact line (the nearest hostile-held state touching own-controlled land, weighed against the divisions already fronting it), drawn again when that state leaves the contact line or the army loses its order. Phases with axes attack as usual. attack written out in a phase with axes: [] makes it an attack phase, not a hold: each army takes its layout axis, its victory-point row or the nearest target

prepare_against.description: country tags a coming war is declared on (set it in the phase before the declaration): at peace with all of them, the armies draw their fronts and offensive lines on them as in a hold phase and plan, nothing executes, so the first day of the war only gives the execute order

burst_orders.description: orders one tick's war burst may give: the war step is called again within the tick until no army has an order left, so every army gets its order in the tick that needs it

burst_hours.description: game hours after which a tick's war burst of mouse orders gives the tick back (the rest go in the next tick), so one burst never holds the calendar for days

burst_seconds.description: wall seconds of input after which a tick's war burst ends (the rest go in the next tick)

guard_reach.description: map units around a guard's post (and a reserve army's state) within which it faces enemy-held land; land bordering the post always counts. A guard with no enemy in reach stands ready

defend_per_state.description: posture defend: divisions one stretch of the contact line takes per own state touching it before the next army is sent to a less crowded stretch (the game's own defenders hold two to four a province)

hold_prepares.description: in a hold phase (axes: []) the armies still draw their front and offensive line toward their next target and plan on them; only the execute order waits for a phase with axes, and a plan still executing on enemy land is stopped. false: a hold phase draws no line on enemy land

planning_wait.description: after an offensive line is drawn, the execute order waits for the planning bonus: read from hoi4_armies planning.mean (executes at planning_share of planning_cap, or once the bonus stops rising for a game day), else estimated from game days; false executes the next tick

planning_cap.description: the army's maximum planning bonus (share, 0.30 or 30)

planning_share.description: share of planning_cap the bonus must reach before execution

planning_gain.description: planning bonus gained per game day

planning_max_days.description: longest planning wait in game days

planning_flat_days.description: an offensive planned again (a stopped plan, a rest) executes once its planning bonus has stood still this many game days below the wanted level: divisions in contact or on the move build none

planning_skip_days.description: no planning wait when the goal deadline is closer than this many game days

supply_hold.description: supply percent below which nothing attacks, own-state retakes included, and a rest does not end at rest_max_days

supply_resume.description: supply percent at or above which a rested army resumes (never below supply_floor)

rest_below_pct.description: rest below this share of the army's highest organisation seen

resume_above_pct.description: resume at this share of the army's highest organisation seen

pocket_share.description: share of the land provinces around an army held by others at which it falls back from a forming pocket (outside fully held own states)

pocket_reach.description: farthest distance (map units between state centres) a pocket fall-back goes; an army_layout role falls back only into its own state, axis or guard states

encircle.description: encirclement operations (default on; false switches them off): find an enemy pocket worth closing (hoi4_encirclement_candidates), commit two driven armies as pincers into its neck with a battle plan and the planning wait, launch both together, hold the ring with one arm and reduce the pocket with the other, then resume the advance; give up a pocket that would break supply or is not closed in time. Never in a hold phase (axes []) or with direct_moves

boldness.description: sets the defaults below: cautious (gap 1, score 4, reach 100, the full arm strength, supply 80+, abort at the supply floor, 20 days to close, one driven army kept free, no coastal pocket), measured (gap 2, score 2, reach 160, 75% of the arm strength, supply at supply_resume, abort at supply_hold, 30 days), bold (gap 3, score 1, reach 260, half the arm strength, supply at the floor, no supply abort, 45 days)

max_gap.description: neck states a pocket may need taken

min_score.description: the candidate read's score (pocket value per effort) a pocket needs; a pocket already cut off is always reduced

reach.description: map units from an army's state centre to its arm's own state; farther armies are not pulled across the theatre

need_share.description: share of an arm's divisions_needed the committed army must have

min_supply.description: supply percent (or share) an army needs to be committed

abort_supply.description: supply percent below which a closing arm ends the operation; false: no supply abort (the war step's rest rules still apply)

close_max_days.description: game days the neck may take to close before the pocket is given up

keep_free.description: driven armies never committed to an operation

sea_escape.description: accept a pocket with a coast (the enemy may evacuate by sea)

sync_days.description: game days a ready pincer waits for the other arm before it goes alone

reduce.description: after the ring closes the larger arm attacks the pocket, nearest state first; false: both arms hold

retry_days.description: game days a given-up pocket is not tried again

scan_days.description: game days between candidate reads while no operation runs

armies.description: army names or army_layout name_hints that may be committed; empty or absent: any driven army

second_direction.description: the first stall on a target brings a second direction (an idle army beside the target, else this army goes round and redraws); false goes straight to the direct move

bound.description: after a target with an own supply hub, port or railway falls, the army's next advance waits for supply there to recover; false turns it off

bound_rail_days.description: game days a captured railway is dead (the bound ends after it once supply is at the floor)

bound_core_days.description: the same in an own (core) state

bound_max_days.description: longest bound pause in game days

supply_relief.description: an army below supply_floor gets a railway to the own railway node nearest where it starves, then one more motorization level; false: report only

relief_after_days.description: game days below supply_floor before the supply relief acts

relief_report_days.description: game days below supply_floor before the spell is reported (alarm army_out_of_supply)

move_commit_days.description: an army keeps a move this many game days against every other step (a pocket fall-back is exempt)

move_budget.description: at most this many moves per army in move_window_days (each move costs organisation)

overrides.description: Keys merged over the base plan while a phase or contingency is active (top-level keys replaced, war merged key by key). Executor support is build item 15.

slot_empty_grace_days.description: game days research_slot_empty and no_active_focus wait while the plan lists what the executor starts there (research_path / research_priority, focus_path / focus_fallback): a slot the executor fills at its next tick is not reported, and a list that ran out raises the plan-exhausted alarm instead

why.description: Free text for people and the player; never read by the executor. Names every alarm this object switches off and the reason (lint alarms.silenced).

note.description: Free text for people and the player; never read by the executor.

alarms.description: Alarm thresholds (native/src/alarms.rs table); any alarm code set to false is silenced, and `why` then names it with the reason (lint alarms.silenced).

army.description: army_layout name_hint or a substring of an army name; empty: any army

order.description: position in the planned sequence: the lint orders its estimates by it, the executor takes the targets in list order, so write the list in this order

vp.description: victory points of the province, checked against the state history; the surrender estimate counts them

by.description: planned date: the lint places captures and construction triggers by it; the executor has no date per target (use checkpoints for a date that must hold)

path.description: waypoint provinces in order from own land to the target (the target last or left out), each touching the next. The executor follows it leg by leg: the first waypoint it does not hold is the next objective, attacked from the held waypoint before it, and the next leg starts only once the army's supply is back at war.supply_resume (at most war.rest_max_days above war.supply_hold). A waypoint held by a country it is not at war with closes the path: the executor then routes on its own and says so in the run result's war notes (route:<army>). Without a path the executor routes on its own

from.description: provinces the attack is expected to start from; the lint counts them as part of the route, the executor starts a leg from the held waypoint before it (see path)

why.description: Free text for people and the player; never read by the executor.

note.description: Free text for people and the player; never read by the executor.

running_vp.description: enemy VP held after this target (start control, this target and the ones before it, paths included); the lint checks it

reserve.description: true: past the goal.capitulation aim, taken only if the threshold has not been lowered as planned; the executor takes it like any other target, so list reserves after the main set

states.description: state ids, numeric strings or exact state names

why.description: Free text for people and the player; never read by the executor.

note.description: Free text for people and the player; never read by the executor.

order.description: done-memory key when the item has no id (plan_run.rs construction_plan_step)

building.description: building key; rail_way or railway uses hoi4_railway_build

path.description: railway: first and last provinces are the end points

legs.description: railway with both ends (from_state/to_state or path): the target may lie beyond own control; the way between the ends is computed from the map files (existing railways preferred) and each send lays the own-controlled part of it (hoi4_railway_build leg); the item is sent again every leg_days until the railway stands to the target. Default false

leg_days.description: game days between two legs of a `legs` railway (default 14)

when.description: a trigger (date, province_controlled, state_fully_controlled, owner) or any plan predicate (e.g. tech_researched:radio_detection); the item is queued once it holds

requires.description: technologies the building needs (enable_building level 1; facts.py support <TAG>): the item waits for all of them without spending its three tries (radar_station needs radio_detection, which the sp_air_radar project grants)

why.description: Free text for people and the player; never read by the executor.

note.description: Free text for people and the player; never read by the executor.

cap.description: never more than this many divisions of the template fielded plus queued

only_if_stockpile.description: archetype (or variant key) -> equipment the stockpile must hold: training waits while hoi4_stockpile holds less (without that read, while a fielded division lacks that archetype); every archetype not named here waits for one batch's need of a fielded division of the template

note.description: Free text for people and the player; never read by the executor.

armies.description: purpose exercise only: army names or army_layout name_hints that exercise (none: every own army)

ref.description: the plan item paid for: template:<templates id>, doctrine:<doctrines id>, design:<id>, spirit:<idea>

note.description: Free text for people and the player; never read by the executor.

xp_spends.description: ordered spends of one experience pool (pools cap at 500)

states.description: conquest: the states taken for this resource

refineries.description: synthetic: refineries built by `by` (rubber per refinery from the building and the research path's techs)

until.description: the date the source ends (a deficit's end, a trade the coming war closes)

regions.description: added to the fleet's area first (hoi4_fleet_region)

task_force.description: only this task force (absent: every task force of the fleet)
